messages:
maria: quick question — are we double-billing when a client disconnects mid-stream and then reconnects to resume? seeing some customers complain about spikes.
akash: short answer: currently we charge per-token emitted by the runtime. reconnects can cause duplicate sends if resume logic isn't deduped.
tom: can we rely on stream_id + resume_offset to dedupe on the billing side? that's what we do for model state, but billing is in a different service.
julie: billing service only gets events: chunk_emitted (stream_id, token_count), stream_closed (stream_id). if a client reconnects we currently emit new chunk_emitted events. no dedupe today.
samir: two main options: 1) make billing idempotent by including client-supplied resume_offset and server-side highest_offset_committed, 2) change runtime to emit tentative vs committed counts and only commit on final close/idle timeout. both have tradeoffs.
maria: tradeoffs = fraud vector vs UX. if we only bill on commit, a malicious client could hold streams open and not commit to avoid payment.
akash: we can add a small precharge / reserved token model: reserve N tokens (e.g., 512) at stream start, bill incremental committed tokens beyond that, refund unused reserved on close. avoids large out-of-band holes.
julie: implementation note: runtime can emit events: stream_started(stream_id, reserved=512), chunk_committed(stream_id, offset, count), stream_final(stream_id), stream_abandoned(stream_id, timeout). billing listens and adjusts.
tom: pseudocode for idempotent billing logic:```python
# billing consumer
if event.type == 'chunk_committed':
  key = event.stream_id + ':' + str(event.offset)
  if not seen(key):
    bill(event.org, event.count)
    mark_seen(key)
```
works but needs bounded retention of seen keys.
samir: retention can be TTL of 24h for seen chunk keys, plus occasional GC. We'll also store highest_committed_offset per stream to do range dedupe cheaply.
maria: what about resumed partial tokens where client acks only until last delivered token? clients might not ACK.
julie: we already send explicit end-of-stream marker when model finishes; but in long-running streams clients often drop. runtime should detect client disconnect and mark stream_abandoned after grace window, commit whatever was emitted server-side.
akash: telemetry-wise we need metrics: active_streams, reserved_tokens_total, reserved_tokens_unused_refunded, resumed_streams_count, duplicate_token_attempts, billed_tokens, produced_tokens.
telemetry-bot: note: add events to pipeline with these fields -> stream_id, org_id, key_id, event_type, token_count, offset, result_status. correlate with billing_tx_id for audit.
samir: console UX: add per-key streaming panel showing "reserved vs billed" and "resumed rate". let customers set their own burst reservation size and grace timeout.
maria: security: per-org limits should trump per-key to avoid a single key using org burst. policy: allowance = min(org_burst_remaining, key_burst_limit).
tom: rollout plan: feature off by default. enable for 10% canary orgs, monitor duplicate_token_attempts and customer support tickets.
julie: alerting: fire if duplicate_token_attempts > 0.5% of produced_tokens in a 1h window, or if reserved_tokens_unused_refunded ratio > 30% (indicates configuration mismatch).
akash: edge case: cross-region resume where client reconnects to different region behind routing. need global stream_id and central resume table or signed resume tokens.
maria: signed resume token proposal: runtime issues resume_token = HMAC(stream_id | region | expiry) given to client; on reconnect any region can validate and ask billing to dedupe using the canonical stream_id.
samir: storage ops: resume table should be small objects keyed by stream_id with highest_offset and reserved_amount; TTL 48h. fine to replicate via regional cache with fallback to control plane.
julie: UX detail: console should show an example header for clients: "X-Resume-Token: <token>" and example reconnect flow.
maria: can we also expose per-route telemetry for streaming so product teams can see which routes cause most resumes/duplicates?
akash: yes — per-route labels on events. also track median resume latency and percent of streams resumed within 30s.
telemetry-bot: added to backlog: create events schema PR (#issue-5823) and add billing consumer changes (#issue-5824).
ops-bot: deploy window request: these changes touch runtime, billing, telemetry. propose small iterative deploy: 1) telemetry events only, 2) billing idempotency + reserved token prototype, 3) runtime resume-token issuance and dedupe. Can we do step 2 in the next sprint? :calendar:
maria: agree on iterative. I'll draft RFC with the designs above and canary plan. anyone want to pair on the RFC?
tom: I'll take the billing idempotency section. akash will own telemetry schema. julie will own runtime changes. samir will own console dashboards.
maria: thanks team. will post RFC link shortly. :thumbsup:
